subproblems.title: Exhaustion of an open set by compactly contained open sets
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ and every open set U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Eucl P) there is a sequence (W_i)_{i∈ℕ} of subsets of ℝ^P with two properties. (a) For every i, CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U holds: W_i is open, closure(W_i) is compact and closure(W_i) ⊆ U. (b) Every compact K ⊆ U is contained in W_i for some i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∃ W : ℕ → Set (Eucl P), (∀ i, CompactlyContainedOpen (W i) U) ∧ ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ i, K ⊆ W i
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 1 (exhaustion). The parent's condition B̄_{1/i}(x) ⊆ U is expressed here through the extended distance to ℝ^P∖U, so no convention for dist(x, ∅) is needed. The index is shifted to avoid 1/0.

Notation: |x| is the Euclidean norm on ℝ^P = Eucl P. For x ∈ ℝ^P let d(x) := inf{edist(x, y) : y ∈ ℝ^P∖U} ∈ [0, ∞] (Lean: Metric.infEDist x Uᶜ). If U = ℝ^P then d ≡ ∞.

1. d is continuous (Metric.continuous_infEDist). Since ℝ^P∖U is closed (U is open), d(x) = 0 iff x ∈ closure(ℝ^P∖U) = ℝ^P∖U (Metric.mem_closure_iff_infEDist_zero). In particular d(x) > 0 for every x ∈ U.
2. For i ∈ ℕ define W_i := {x : |x| < i} ∩ {x : (i+1)⁻¹ < d(x)}, where (i+1)⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞).
3. W_i is open: it is the intersection of the preimages of the open sets (−∞, i) and ((i+1)⁻¹, ∞] under the continuous maps x ↦ |x| and d.
4. W_i ⊆ B̄_i(0), and B̄_i(0) is closed, so closure(W_i) ⊆ B̄_i(0). B̄_i(0) is compact because ℝ^P is proper, so closure(W_i) is compact as a closed subset of a compact set.
5. F_i := {x : (i+1)⁻¹ ≤ d(x)} is closed (d is continuous) and contains W_i, so closure(W_i) ⊆ F_i. Suppose some x ∈ closure(W_i) is not in U. Then d(x) = 0 by Step 1, while x ∈ F_i gives d(x) ≥ (i+1)⁻¹ > 0 (since i+1 < ∞), a contradiction. Hence closure(W_i) ⊆ U. Together with Steps 3 and 4, CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U holds for every i.
6. Let K ⊆ U be compact. If K = ∅ then K ⊆ W_0. Otherwise:
- K is bounded, so there is R ∈ ℝ with |x| ≤ R for all x ∈ K. Choose i₁ ∈ ℕ with i₁ > R.
- d is continuous and K is compact and nonempty, so d attains its minimum on K at some x₀ ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Since x₀ ∈ U, Step 1 gives m := d(x₀) > 0.
- Choose i₂ ∈ ℕ with (i₂)⁻¹ < m (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt).
- Put i := max(i₁, i₂). For x ∈ K we have |x| ≤ R < i₁ ≤ i and (i+1)⁻¹ ≤ (i₂)⁻¹ < m ≤ d(x), so x ∈ W_i. Hence K ⊆ W_i.
7. Steps 5 and 6 show that (W_i)_{i∈ℕ} has both required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: d(x) := infEDist(x, ℝ^P∖U) is continuous and vanishes exactly off U.
W_i := {|x| < i} ∩ {d > (i+1)⁻¹} is open.
closure W_i ⊆ closedBall(0,i) ∩ {d ≥ (i+1)⁻¹}, which is compact and contained in U.
A compact K ⊆ U is bounded and min_K d > 0, so K ⊆ W_i for large i.

subproblems.title: Mass estimate |T(ω)| ≤ M_W(T)·sup|ω| for test forms supported in W
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (B C : ℝ), 0 ≤ B → T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → |T ω| ≤ B * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 2 (basic mass estimate). It is stated with an explicit real bound B for M_W(T) and an explicit pointwise bound C for |ω|, which avoids dividing by sup|ω| and any case distinction on ω = 0.

Notation: for an n-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P, I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ψ)) over ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ψ ⊆ W and |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and a covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|. Each coefficient satisfies (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so the sum of squares is multiplied by t², and √(t²S) = |t|·√S.
2. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C.
3. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix a real c > C, so c > 0. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}. TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, so s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Also tsupport(s•ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and by Step 1, |(s•ω)(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ C/c ≤ 1 for every x. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(T(s•ω)) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B.
4. (Unpacking.) Because B ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B implies a ≤ B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff). By linearity T(s•ω) = s·T(ω). Therefore c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B and −c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B. Multiplying by c > 0 gives T(ω) ≤ Bc and −T(ω) ≤ Bc, i.e. |T(ω)| ≤ B·c. This holds for every c > C.
5. (Letting c ↓ C.) Let ε > 0 and c := C + ε/(B+1) > C. Step 4 gives |T(ω)| ≤ BC + Bε/(B+1) ≤ BC + ε. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, |T(ω)| ≤ B·C (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: |tα| = |t|·|α| and C ≥ 0.
For c > C, ±c⁻¹ω is mass-admissible for W, so ±c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B by le_massOn and B ≥ 0.
Hence |T(ω)| ≤ B·c for every c > C; let c decrease to C.

subproblems.title: Coordinate expansion of covectors in the basis dx^β
subproblems.statement:
For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n:
α = Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β,
where I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P is the finite type of order embeddings β : Fin n ↪o Fin P, α(e_β) = euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β = α(e_{β(0)},…,e_{β(n−1)}) with e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, and dx^β = wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n), α = ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β • wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Fact A in the parent proof's conventions (an alternating n-linear map is determined by its values on increasing tuples of basis vectors, and dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}), proved here in full.

Notation:
- e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply).
- For a tuple v : Fin n → Fin P, e_v := (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}).
- I(n,P) := SimonMultiIndex n P = Fin n ↪o Fin P, a finite type.
- For β ∈ I(n,P), α(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β and dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).

1. (Kronecker property.) Let β, γ ∈ I(n,P). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^β(e_γ) = det M, where M_{ij} = proj(β(i))(e_{γ(j)}) is 1 if β(i) = γ(j) and 0 otherwise.
(a) If β = γ, then M_{ij} = 1 iff β(i) = β(j) iff i = j (β is injective). So M is the identity matrix and dx^β(e_β) = 1.
(b) If β ≠ γ, there is i with β(i) ∉ {γ(0),…,γ(n−1)}. Otherwise range β ⊆ range γ. Both ranges have exactly n elements because β and γ are injective (Set.ncard_range_of_injective), so range β = range γ (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le). An order embedding of the well-order Fin n is determined by its range (OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so β = γ, a contradiction. For this i, row i of M is zero, hence det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).
Thus dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}.
2. (Agreement on increasing tuples.) Let R := Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β, a continuous alternating n-linear map. For γ ∈ I(n,P), Step 1 gives R(e_γ) = Σ_β α(e_β)·δ_{βγ} = α(e_γ).
3. (Agreement on injective tuples.) Let v : Fin n → Fin P be injective, and let σ := Tuple.sort v, a permutation of Fin n with v∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). Since v∘σ is also injective, it is strictly increasing, so γ := v∘σ defines an element of I(n,P) (OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono) with e_γ = e_v∘σ. For every alternating map f, f(e_v∘σ) = sign(σ)·f(e_v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Applying this to α and to R and using Step 2 gives sign(σ)·α(e_v) = α(e_γ) = R(e_γ) = sign(σ)·R(e_v). Acting with sign(σ)⁻¹ (inv_smul_smul) yields α(e_v) = R(e_v).
4. (Conclusion.) Two alternating multilinear maps on ℝ^P that agree on all tuples (e_{v(0)},…,e_{v(n−1)}) with v injective are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis). Hence α and R are equal as alternating maps, and therefore as continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). So α = Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β.
5. (Degenerate cases.) Steps 1–4 cover them. For n = 0, I(0,P) has one element, dx^β is the constant covector 1, and the identity reads α = α(())·1. For n > P, I(n,P) is empty, so R = 0, and no injective v exists, so Step 4 gives α = 0 = R. ∎
proof_key_steps: dx^β(e_γ) = det[δ_{β(i)γ(j)}] = δ_{βγ} for increasing β, γ.
R := Σ_β α(e_β)dx^β agrees with α on increasing basis tuples.
Sorting an injective tuple (Tuple.sort, AlternatingMap.map_perm) gives agreement on all injective basis tuples.
Module.Basis.ext_alternating gives α = R.

subproblems.title: Countable sup-norm-dense families of test forms supported in a relatively compact set
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)), IsCompact (closure W) → ∃ E : Set (TestFormOn U n), E.Countable ∧ (∀ η ∈ E, tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ η ∈ E, ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x - (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 3 (countable dense families). It is carried out through coefficient vectors, so only the finite-dimensional space ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P) is needed. Covector (Eucl P) n has no FiniteDimensional or SecondCountableTopology instance at this Mathlib pin.

Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; 𝓘 := Fin n → Fin P and N := #𝓘. ℝ^𝓘 carries the sup norm ‖·‖_∞.

1. (Coefficient map.) Define c : Covector (Eucl P) n → ℝ^𝓘 by c(α) := (α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)}))_{I∈𝓘}. Each coordinate of c is evaluation at a fixed tuple, so c is linear and continuous. Since |c(α)_I| ≤ ‖c(α)‖_∞ (norm_le_pi_norm), |α|² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} c(α)_I² ≤ N·‖c(α)‖_∞². Hence |α| ≤ √N·‖c(α)‖_∞.
2. (Embedding.) Let K := closure(W), which is compact by hypothesis; regard it as a compact metric space. Let D := {ω ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ω ⊆ W}. For ω ∈ D define F_ω ∈ C(K, ℝ^𝓘) by F_ω(x) := c(ω(x)). It is continuous because ω is smooth, hence continuous, and c is continuous.
3. (Second countability.) C(K, ℝ^𝓘) is second countable: K is compact and metrizable, hence second countable and locally compact, and ℝ^𝓘 is second countable (ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology, Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/SecondCountableSpace.lean). Its topology is given by the sup metric, and dist(F(x), G(x)) ≤ dist(F, G) for x ∈ K (ContinuousMap.dist_apply_le_dist).
4. (Countable dense subset of the image.) The set A := {F_ω : ω ∈ D} is separable (TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.of_separableSpace). Since C(K, ℝ^𝓘) is metrizable, there is a countable S ⊆ A with A ⊆ closure(S) (TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.exists_countable_dense_subset).
5. (Definition of E.) For every s ∈ S choose ω_s ∈ D with F_{ω_s} = s, and let E := {ω_s : s ∈ S}. E is countable, being the range of a map on the countable set S. Also E ⊆ D, so every η ∈ E belongs to TestFormOn U n and has tsupport η ⊆ W.
6. (Density.) Let ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W (so ω ∈ D), let ε > 0, and put δ := ε/(√N + 1) > 0. Since F_ω ∈ closure(S), there is s ∈ S with dist(F_ω, s) < δ. Let η := ω_s ∈ E, so F_η = s.
- For x ∈ K: by linearity of c, ‖c(ω(x) − η(x))‖_∞ = ‖F_ω(x) − F_η(x)‖_∞ ≤ dist(F_ω, F_η) < δ. By Step 1, |ω(x) − η(x)| ≤ √N·δ ≤ ε.
- For x ∉ K: x ∉ tsupport ω and x ∉ tsupport η, since both are ⊆ W ⊆ K. So ω(x) = η(x) = 0 and |ω(x) − η(x)| = 0 ≤ ε. ∎
proof_key_steps: The coefficient map c : Covector → ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P) is continuous and linear, with |α| ≤ √N·‖c(α)‖_∞.
ω ↦ c∘ω embeds D_W into C(closure W, ℝ^(Fin n → Fin P)), which is second countable.
Take a countable dense subset of the image and choose preimages to form E ⊆ D_W.
Sup-distance < δ on closure W gives |ω − η| ≤ ε everywhere, since both forms vanish off closure W.

subproblems.title: Uniform approximation of continuous compactly supported forms by test forms
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let U, V ⊆ ℝ^P with V open and V ⊆ U. Let ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n be continuous with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ V, and let ε > 0. Then there is η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ V and |ω(x) − η(x)| ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V : Set (Eucl P)) (ω : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) n), IsOpen V → V ⊆ U → Continuous ω → HasCompactSupport ω → tsupport ω ⊆ V → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ η : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ V ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the final sentence of parent proof Step 7: a continuous compactly supported form supported in an open set is a uniform limit of test forms supported there, by mollification. Here the mollification is followed by multiplication with a smooth cutoff, which keeps the support exactly inside V.

Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ‖α‖ is the operator norm of α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n; e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; N := #(Fin n → Fin P).

1. (Norm comparison.) For every covector α and every I : Fin n → Fin P, |α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j‖e_{I(j)}‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm and ‖e_i‖ = 1). Hence |α|² ≤ N‖α‖², i.e. |α| ≤ √N‖α‖. Put c := √N + 1 > 0.
2. (Intermediate open set.) K := tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport ω) and K ⊆ V. Choose an open V' with K ⊆ V', closure(V') compact and closure(V') ⊆ V (exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure; ℝ^P is locally compact and regular).
3. (Cutoff.) Choose a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0,1] with support χ = V' and χ(x) = 1 ⇔ x ∈ K (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with the open set V', the closed set K ⊆ V' and smoothness order ⊤). Then tsupport χ = closure(V') ⊆ V, and tsupport χ is compact.
4. (Mollification.) ω is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). Convolving ω with a normalized C^∞ bump of small enough radius gives a C^∞ map g : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n with ‖g(x) − ω(x)‖ < ε/c for every x (UniformContinuous.exists_contDiff_dist_le in Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/BumpFunction/SmoothApprox.lean, whose proof is exactly this convolution). It applies because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional and Covector (Eucl P) n is complete.
5. (The test form.) Let η(x) := χ(x)·g(x).
- η is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul).
- tsupport η ⊆ tsupport χ = closure(V') ⊆ V ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left).
- tsupport η is compact, being a closed subset of the compact set closure(V').
Hence η ∈ TestFormOn U n (smooth, compactly supported, tsupport ⊆ U) and tsupport η ⊆ V.
6. (Estimate.) If x ∈ K, then χ(x) = 1, so ω(x) − η(x) = ω(x) − g(x) and ‖ω(x) − η(x)‖ < ε/c. If x ∉ K, then ω(x) = 0, so ‖ω(x) − η(x)‖ = χ(x)‖g(x)‖ ≤ ‖g(x)‖ = ‖g(x) − ω(x)‖ < ε/c, using 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1. So ‖ω(x) − η(x)‖ ≤ ε/c for every x, and by Step 1, |ω(x) − η(x)| ≤ √N·ε/c ≤ ε. ∎
proof_key_steps: |α| ≤ √N‖α‖ in terms of the operator norm.
Choose V' with tsupport ω ⊆ V' and closure V' ⊆ V compact, and a smooth cutoff χ with χ = 1 exactly on tsupport ω and support χ = V'.
Mollification gives a smooth g with ‖g − ω‖ < ε/c everywhere (UniformContinuous.exists_contDiff_dist_le).
η := χ·g is a test form with tsupport ⊆ V and |ω − η| ≤ ε.

subproblems.title: Weakly convergent subsequence under local mass bounds (Banach–Alaoglu step of 2.15)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let T : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n satisfy sup_q M_W(T_q) < ∞ for every W with CompactlyContainedOpen W U. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and T₀ ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n such that T_{φ(q)} ⇀ T₀ in U, i.e. T_{φ(q)}(ω) → T₀(ω) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n (WeaklyConvergesOn (fun q => T (φ q)) T₀).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ T : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (⨆ q, (T q).massOn W) < ∞) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (T₀ : GeometricCurrentOn U n), StrictMono φ ∧ WeaklyConvergesOn (fun q => T (φ q)) T₀
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Steps 1 and 3–6 (exhaustion, countable dense families, diagonal subsequence, Cauchy extension, limit current); this is the 'Banach–Alaoglu' step of Simon 2.15. Siblings used:
- exhaustion (cmb_exists_compactly_contained_exhaustion);
- mass_bound (cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le);
- testform_separable (cmb_exists_countable_dense_testForms).

Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ‖α‖ is the operator norm of a covector; N := #(Fin n → Fin P); D^n(U) := TestFormOn U n.

0. (Norm comparison.) For every covector α, |α| ≤ √N‖α‖. Each coefficient satisfies |α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j‖e_{I(j)}‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i has norm 1), so |α|² ≤ N‖α‖².
1. (Exhaustion.) By the sibling exhaustion there are sets W_i (i ∈ ℕ) with CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U for every i, such that every compact K ⊆ U lies in some W_i.
2. (Uniform constants.) Let B_i := (sup_q M_{W_i}(T_q)).toReal ≥ 0. By hypothesis sup_q M_{W_i}(T_q) < ∞, so it equals ENNReal.ofReal B_i (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal), and M_{W_i}(T_q) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B_i for every q.
3. (Dense families.) For each i, closure(W_i) is compact, so the sibling testform_separable gives a countable E_i ⊆ D^n(U) such that tsupport η ⊆ W_i for η ∈ E_i, and such that for every ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W_i and every ε > 0 there is η ∈ E_i with |ω(x) − η(x)| ≤ ε for all x. Let E := ⋃_i E_i, which is countable.
4. (Bounds on E.) Every test form η is continuous with compact support, so there is C' with ‖η(x)‖ ≤ C' for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). By Step 0, |η(x)| ≤ C_η := √N·C' for all x. For η ∈ E choose i(η) with η ∈ E_{i(η)}. The sibling mass_bound, with W = W_{i(η)}, B = B_{i(η)} and C = C_η (using Step 2 and tsupport η ⊆ W_{i(η)}), gives |T_q(η)| ≤ b_η := B_{i(η)}·C_η for every q.
5. (Diagonal subsequence.) Put x_q := (T_q(η))_{η∈E} ∈ ℝ^E. Every x_q lies in Q := ∏_{η∈E}[−b_η, b_η], which is compact by Tychonoff (isCompact_univ_pi). ℝ^E is first countable because E is countable. By sequential compactness (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there are a ∈ Q and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with x_{φ(q)} → a. By tendsto_pi_nhds this means T_{φ(q)}(η) → a_η for every η ∈ E. (This is the Bolzano–Weierstrass and Cantor diagonal step of the parent proof.)
6. (Cauchy property on every test form.) Let ω ∈ D^n(U). tsupport ω is compact and contained in U, so tsupport ω ⊆ W_i for some i (Step 1). Let ε > 0 and ε' := ε/(3(B_i + 1)) > 0.
- By Step 3 choose η ∈ E_i with |ω(x) − η(x)| ≤ ε' for all x.
- Then ω − η ∈ D^n(U) and tsupport(ω − η) ⊆ tsupport ω ∪ tsupport η ⊆ W_i (tsupport_sub). So the sibling mass_bound gives |T_q(ω) − T_q(η)| = |T_q(ω − η)| ≤ B_i·ε' ≤ ε/3 for every q.
- The convergent sequence (T_{φ(q)}(η))_q is Cauchy, so there is N₀ with |T_{φ(q)}(η) − T_{φ(N₀)}(η)| < ε/3 for all q ≥ N₀.
- By the triangle inequality, |T_{φ(q)}(ω) − T_{φ(N₀)}(ω)| < ε/3 + ε/3 + ε/3 = ε for q ≥ N₀.
Hence (T_{φ(q)}(ω))_q is a Cauchy sequence of reals, so it converges (cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete). Let L(ω) be its limit.
7. (Linearity.) Let ω, ω' ∈ D^n(U) and t ∈ ℝ. Then T_{φ(q)}(ω + ω') = T_{φ(q)}(ω) + T_{φ(q)}(ω') → L(ω) + L(ω'), and T_{φ(q)}(t•ω) = t·T_{φ(q)}(ω) → t·L(ω). By uniqueness of limits in ℝ (tendsto_nhds_unique), L(ω + ω') = L(ω) + L(ω') and L(t•ω) = t·L(ω). So L is a linear map D^n(U) → ℝ.
8. (Sequential continuity.) Let (ω_j) satisfy TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. Then there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j such that, for every k, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0 uniformly on K. For k = 0 the limit is 0 and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), so sup_{x∈K}‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0. Choose i with K ⊆ W_i (Step 1). Given ε > 0, let δ := ε/(2(B_i + 1)(√N + 1)) > 0.
- For all large j, ‖ω_j(x)‖ < δ for x ∈ K, and ω_j(x) = 0 for x ∉ K. By Step 0, |ω_j(x)| ≤ √N·δ for every x.
- The sibling mass_bound gives |T_{φ(q)}(ω_j)| ≤ B_i·√N·δ for every q.
- Letting q → ∞ gives |L(ω_j)| ≤ B_i·√N·δ ≤ ε/2 < ε (le_of_tendsto').
Thus L(ω_j) → 0.
9. (Conclusion.) By Steps 7 and 8, T₀ := ⟨L, Step 8⟩ is an element of GeometricCurrentOn U n. By Step 6, T_{φ(q)}(ω) → T₀(ω) for every ω ∈ D^n(U), i.e. WeaklyConvergesOn (fun q => T (φ q)) T₀. φ is strictly increasing by Step 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: Exhaustion by W_i ⊂⊂ U; B_i := sup_q M_{W_i}(T_q) is finite.
Countable sup-dense E_i ⊆ D_{W_i}; the mass bound gives |T_q(η)| ≤ b_η on E = ⋃E_i.
Tychonoff and sequential compactness of ∏[−b_η, b_η] give φ with T_{φ(q)}(η) convergent for all η ∈ E.
The mass bound and density make (T_{φ(q)}(ω)) Cauchy for every test form; L(ω) := its limit.
L is linear, and |L(ω_j)| ≤ B_i√N·sup|ω_j| gives sequential continuity, so T₀ := L ∈ D_n(U) and T_{φ(q)} ⇀ T₀.

subproblems.title: Integral representation extends to continuous forms with the mass bound (2.7)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U, W ⊆ ℝ^P with CompactlyContainedOpen W U. Let T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, μ a measure on ℝ^P and v : ℝ^P → NVector (Eucl P) n with IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v. Let B, C ∈ ℝ with B ≥ 0 and T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B. Let ω : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n be continuous with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ C for every x. Then x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and |∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x)| ≤ B·C.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)), CompactlyContainedOpen W U → ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v → ∀ (B C : ℝ), 0 ≤ B → T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B → ∀ ω : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) n, Continuous ω → tsupport ω ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ C) → Integrable (fun x => v x (ω x)) μ ∧ |∫ x, v x (ω x) ∂μ| ≤ B * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 7, the content of 'by 2.7' in the printed text. (a) Testing the representation with χ·dx^β makes the coefficients of v integrable on the relevant compact set. (b) The mass bound passes from test forms to continuous forms by mollification. The parent's dominated-convergence step is replaced by the direct estimate of Step 5 below, which uses the same integrable functions g_β. Siblings used:
- mass_bound (cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le);
- mollify (cmb_exists_testForm_uniform_approx);
- covector_expansion (cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge).

Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; I(n,P) := SimonMultiIndex n P; for β ∈ I(n,P), α(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β and dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)). v(θ) denotes the function x ↦ v(x)(θ(x)).

1. (Facts on |·|.)
(i) |α(e_β)| ≤ |α| for β ∈ I(n,P). Indeed α(e_β)² is the term I = β (strictly increasing; EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i) in the sum of nonnegative terms defining |α|².
(ii) |α + γ| ≤ |α| + |γ|. Indeed |α| is the Euclidean norm of the vector (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_I) else 0)_{I : Fin n → Fin P} ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P), which depends additively on α. Also |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. (Supports.) C ≥ 0 since 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C. K := tsupport ω is closed and contained in the compact set closure(W), hence compact. Since W is open, choose an open V with K ⊆ V, closure(V) compact and closure(V) ⊆ W. Then choose an open V₂ with closure(V) ⊆ V₂, closure(V₂) compact and closure(V₂) ⊆ W (exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure, applied twice).
3. (Cutoff and coefficient functions.) Choose a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0,1] with support χ = V₂ and χ(x) = 1 ⇔ x ∈ closure(V) (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff). Then tsupport χ = closure(V₂) is compact and ⊆ W ⊆ closure(W) ⊆ U. For β ∈ I(n,P) let ψ_β(x) := χ(x)·dx^β. ψ_β is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul with a constant), and tsupport ψ_β ⊆ tsupport χ (tsupport_smul_subset_left), so ψ_β has compact support and tsupport ⊆ U; thus ψ_β ∈ TestFormOn U n. Let g_β(x) := v(x)(ψ_β(x)). By IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v, every g_β is μ-integrable. Put G := Σ_β ∫|g_β| dμ ≥ 0.
4. (Pointwise identity.) Let θ : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n with θ(x) = 0 for every x ∉ closure(V). Then v(x)(θ(x)) = Σ_β θ(x)(e_β)·g_β(x) for every x. If x ∈ closure(V), then χ(x) = 1, so g_β(x) = v(x)(dx^β); the sibling covector_expansion gives θ(x) = Σ_β θ(x)(e_β)·dx^β, and v(x) is linear. If x ∉ closure(V), then θ(x) = 0 and both sides are 0.
5. (Integrability and basic estimate.) Let θ be as in Step 4, continuous, with |θ(x)| ≤ D for all x. For each β, x ↦ θ(x)(e_β) is continuous (evaluation at a fixed tuple), hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable (ℝ^P carries its Borel σ-algebra), and it is bounded by D by Step 1(i). So x ↦ θ(x)(e_β)·g_β(x) is μ-integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul). By Step 4, v(θ) is a finite sum of integrable functions, hence μ-integrable, with ∫v(θ)dμ = Σ_β ∫θ(x)(e_β)g_β(x)dμ (integral_finsetSum). Therefore |∫v(θ)dμ| ≤ Σ_β ∫|θ(x)(e_β)|·|g_β(x)|dμ ≤ D·G.
6. (Integrability of v(ω).) ω vanishes off K ⊆ V ⊆ closure(V) and |ω| ≤ C. By Step 5, x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable, which is the first conclusion.
7. (Approximation.) Let ε > 0. The sibling mollify (V open, V ⊆ U, ω continuous with compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ V) gives η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ V and |ω(x) − η(x)| ≤ ε for all x. Writing η(x) = ω(x) + (−(ω(x) − η(x))), Step 1(ii) gives |η(x)| ≤ C + ε. Since tsupport η ⊆ V ⊆ W and T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B, the sibling mass_bound gives |T(η)| ≤ B(C + ε).
8. (Comparison.) θ := ω − η is continuous, vanishes off closure(V) (both ω and η vanish off V), and |θ(x)| ≤ ε. By Step 5, v(θ) is integrable and |∫v(θ)dμ| ≤ εG. Pointwise v(x)(ω(x)) = v(x)(η(x)) + v(x)(θ(x)), both summands are integrable, and ∫v(η)dμ = T(η) (IsMeasureRepresentation). Hence |∫v(ω)dμ| ≤ |T(η)| + |∫v(θ)dμ| ≤ B(C + ε) + εG.
9. (Conclusion.) For ε₀ > 0, apply Step 8 with ε := ε₀/(B + G + 1): |∫v(ω)dμ| ≤ BC + ε(B + G) ≤ BC + ε₀. As ε₀ > 0 is arbitrary, |∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x)| ≤ B·C (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: Cutoff χ = 1 on closure V ⊇ tsupport ω with tsupport χ ⊆ W; g_β := v(χ·dx^β) is μ-integrable.
Covector expansion: v(x)(θ(x)) = Σ_β θ(x)(e_β)·g_β(x) for θ vanishing off closure V.
Hence v(θ) is integrable with |∫v(θ)dμ| ≤ sup|θ|·Σ_β‖g_β‖₁; in particular v(ω) is integrable.
Mollify ω to η (tsupport ⊆ V, |ω − η| ≤ ε); the mass bound gives |T(η)| ≤ B(C + ε).
|∫v(ω)dμ| ≤ |T(η)| + |∫v(ω − η)dμ| ≤ B(C + ε) + εG; let ε → 0.

subproblems.title: Weak convergence with local mass bounds implies convergence on continuous forms
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (S₀ : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (⨆ q, (S q).massOn W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn S S₀ → ∀ ω : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) n, Continuous ω → HasCompactSupport ω → tsupport ω ⊆ U → ∀ (μ : ℕ → Measure (Eucl P)) (v : ℕ → Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (μ₀ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v₀ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), (∀ q, IsMeasureRepresentation (S q) (μ q) (v q)) → IsMeasureRepresentation S₀ μ₀ v₀ → Tendsto (fun q => ∫ x, v q x (ω x) ∂(μ q)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, v₀ x (ω x) ∂μ₀))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 8, together with the lower-semicontinuity part of Step 6 (Simon 2.14). This is the printed observation that, under local mass bounds, distribution convergence implies convergence on continuous compactly supported forms. Siblings used:
- mollify (cmb_exists_testForm_uniform_approx);
- repr_bound (cmb_measureRepresentation_continuous_bound).

Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. For a representation (μ', v') and a form θ, v'(θ) denotes x ↦ v'(x)(θ(x)).

1. (A compactly contained neighbourhood of the support.) tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport ω) and contained in the open set U. So there is an open W with tsupport ω ⊆ W, closure(W) compact and closure(W) ⊆ U (exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure). Thus CompactlyContainedOpen W U.
2. (Mass constants.) Let B := (sup_q M_W(S_q)).toReal ≥ 0. By hypothesis sup_q M_W(S_q) < ∞, so it equals ENNReal.ofReal B and M_W(S_q) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B for every q. By lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence (Simon 2.14, WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf), M_W(S₀) ≤ liminf_q M_W(S_q) ≤ limsup_q M_W(S_q) ≤ sup_q M_W(S_q) = ENNReal.ofReal B (liminf_le_limsup, limsup_le_iSup).
3. (Approximating test form.) Let ε > 0 and δ := ε/(2B + 2) > 0. Apply the sibling mollify with V := W (W is open, W ⊆ closure(W) ⊆ U, and tsupport ω ⊆ W). It gives η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ W and |ω(x) − η(x)| ≤ δ for every x.
4. (Remainder.) Let ω' := ω − η. It is continuous (η is smooth), tsupport ω' ⊆ tsupport ω ∪ tsupport η ⊆ W (tsupport_sub), and |ω'(x)| ≤ δ for all x. Apply the sibling repr_bound with bound B and C := δ to ω' twice:
- with S_q and (μ_q, v_q), using M_W(S_q) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B;
- with S₀ and (μ₀, v₀), using Step 2.
This gives: v_q(ω') and v₀(ω') are integrable, |∫v_q(ω')dμ_q| ≤ Bδ for every q, and |∫v₀(ω')dμ₀| ≤ Bδ.
5. (Splitting the integrals.) Let (T, μ', v') be either (S_q, μ_q, v_q) or (S₀, μ₀, v₀). By linearity of v'(x), v'(x)(ω(x)) = v'(x)(η(x)) + v'(x)(ω'(x)). v'(η) is integrable with ∫v'(η)dμ' = T(η) (IsMeasureRepresentation), and v'(ω') is integrable (Step 4). Hence ∫v'(ω)dμ' = T(η) + ∫v'(ω')dμ' (integral_add).
6. (Estimate.) Since S_q ⇀ S₀, S_q(η) → S₀(η), so there is N with |S_q(η) − S₀(η)| < δ for all q ≥ N. For q ≥ N, Steps 4 and 5 give
|∫v_q(ω)dμ_q − ∫v₀(ω)dμ₀| ≤ |S_q(η) − S₀(η)| + |∫v_q(ω')dμ_q| + |∫v₀(ω')dμ₀| < δ + 2Bδ = (2B + 1)ε/(2B + 2) < ε.
7. (Conclusion.) As ε > 0 was arbitrary, ∫ v_q(x)(ω(x)) dμ_q(x) → ∫ v₀(x)(ω(x)) dμ₀(x) (Metric.tendsto_atTop). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose an open W ⊂⊂ U containing tsupport ω; B := sup_q M_W(S_q) is finite, and M_W(S₀) ≤ B by 2.14.
Mollify: a test form η with tsupport ⊆ W and |ω − η| ≤ δ.
Representation bound: |∫v_q(ω − η)dμ_q| and |∫v₀(ω − η)dμ₀| are ≤ Bδ, and ∫v'(ω)dμ' = T(η) + ∫v'(ω − η)dμ'.
S_q(η) → S₀(η) gives |∫v_q(ω)dμ_q − ∫v₀(ω)dμ₀| < (2B + 1)δ < ε eventually.
